Every connector returns [] (not raise) when its fixture is absent or the transport errors (test_connectors_degrade).
all_connectors(settings) returns them in display-priority order and omits fec/courtlistener (test_all_connectors_order).
tests/fixtures/http/ contains a recorded, redacted response per connector for a SYNTHETIC/FICTIONAL person - no real people.

tickets.title: The resolver accepts the target, rejects same-name decoys, and the real LLM client conforms to the double
tickets.objective: Correctness is the top priority and this is where it is decided: a Wikidata/strong-key anchored, per-document LLM verdict with hard negative-evidence vetoes, plus the production LLMClient.
acceptance: llm/client.py AnthropicClient implements LLMClient.structured with temperature 0, JSON-schema output, cached system prefix, one retry on invalid JSON then LLMError; test_client_conforms asserts both AnthropicClient and LLMDouble satisfy the Protocol; test_client_parses uses a stubbed SDK response.

resolve(person, docs, llm) returns resolved only when (a) a strong key is found (QID matched on name+detail, company domain from detail, GitHub profile matching name+company, SEC CIK on name+company) OR (b) >=2 yes verdicts citing DIFFERENT disambiguators; otherwise unresolved with empty accepted_doc_ids.
Any verdict `no` whose evidence asserts a conflicting employer/city hard-rejects that doc even if the name matches (test_negative_evidence_vetoes).

tests/fixtures/resolve_cases/ holds >=3 synthetic cases, one mirroring the SPEC Q1 decoy pattern (same name, different profession, one deceased) using FICTIONAL text; test_resolver_cases passes all, including one that must come out unresolved.
Every Verdict.evidence is checked as a substring of the doc text (via util.normalize_ws); verdicts failing this are downgraded to unsure.

tickets.title: The extractor emits schema-valid facts and hubs, and drops any fact whose quote is not in its source
tickets.objective: Turn accepted documents into <=200-char cited facts and canonical hubs, with a mechanical citation check as the hallucination guard, so everything downstream can trust Fact.provenance.
acceptance: extract(person, resolution, docs, llm) calls llm.structured per accepted doc (or per batch <=3 docs) with an internal ExtractionResult schema and returns (facts, hubs) conforming to contracts; test_extract_shapes with LLMDouble.

Citation check: a fact whose provenance.quote is not a normalize_ws substring of its doc's text is DROPPED and counted; test_citation_drop feeds one good and one fabricated quote and asserts only the good fact survives.

Hubs are canonical: hub_id = 'wd:Q...' when the hub came from a wikidata doc carrying the QID, else f'{type}:{slug(label)}'; the same label across two docs yields ONE Hub with merged evidence_fact_ids; DESIGN Decision 3 stop-hubs are never emitted.
recency is set from published_at: 1.0 within 12 months, 0.6 within 3 years, 0.3 otherwise, 0.5 when unknown.
Facts from non-obvious-eligible source kinds are labelled category='non_obvious' when the LLM flags them as not-bio-page material, else their natural category.

tickets.title: Matching ranks rare shared hubs above generic ones and exposes the score components and path
tickets.objective: The user's interest-graph idea made concrete: people as leaves, hubs as centres, IDF-weighted shared hubs produce a 0-100 score with visible components and a graph path as the 'why'.
acceptance: build_graph(dossiers) returns a bipartite nx.Graph with nodes person:{id} and hub:{hub_id}, per-edge recency, per-hub-node idf and type_boost, edge cost=1/(1+idf); a pair's contribution uses min of the two edge recencies; excluded facts' hubs are still included.

IDF per DESIGN Decision 3 with clamp at 0; with the four fixture dossiers, match(g,'charlie',['alpha','bravo','delta']) ranks delta first and its top contribution hub is the rare investor hub; match(g,'alpha',['bravo']) yields score 0 with all-zero contributions.
Match.contributions is sorted desc and sum(c.contribution) == raw before normalisation; Match.path is the weighted shortest path via cost and passes through the top hub.
Match.why is a DETERMINISTIC template naming up to two top hubs by label (no LLM).
Normalisation per Decision 3 against REF = ln(N/3)*1.5: charlie-delta scores 100 and alpha-bravo scores 0; score in [0,100]; the arriving person is never in the output; every present person is.

tickets.title: The digest builder enforces every cap, cites every fact, and always yields a say-out-loud line within 2.5 s
tickets.objective: Assemble a Digest a host can read in ninety seconds: hard caps, displayable-only facts, exactly one non-obvious fact, one invitation-style opener with timeout fallback, and a numbered source list covering every shown fact.
acceptance: make_digest(dossier, matches, llm) returns len(meet) <= 3, len(lately) <= 3, lately sorted by published_at desc and containing only is_displayable facts, non_obvious chosen per DESIGN Data models eligibility (or None), who_line built from current_work facts.

sources contains every Provenance referenced by the facts behind who_line, lately, non_obvious, and - for each Meet row - the arriving person's facts named in contributions[*].hub.evidence_fact_ids, deduped by doc_id, in first-use order.

say_out_loud is produced by ONE llm.structured call whose output is validated to start with Ask/Ask about/Curious and to contain no first-person surveillance phrasing (I saw, we noticed, our records); on timeout (>2.5 s) or validation failure it falls back to f'Ask about {hook.text}'.
exclusion_policy == taste.EXCLUSION_POLICY and meet == [] is represented (not padded) when no one else is present.
Speakability (R18): who_line, each meet[*].why, and say_out_loud contain no http, no [n] markers, no parentheses, no digits used as a score, and are <= 30 words each.

scheduling_constraints: HOURS.md is ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED (intake divergence). EXECUTION.md 8 declares it append-only and ownership-exempt; that makes it a shared write surface every ticket touches, which is exactly the collision the per-file predicate exists to prevent. The orchestrator appends one line per ticket at merge time. No worker writes it.
src/arrival/__main__.py is owned by T-0 (stub) and then T-6 (fills `build`). T-0 closes before any dispatch, so the two are never in flight together.
README.md is owned by T-0 (skeleton) and then T-9 (final). Same reasoning.
tests/fixtures/http/ is split by filename prefix: T-0 owns fixture_dossier_docs_*.json, T-1 owns {kind}_*.json. Disjoint, and T-0 closes first.

src/arrival/contracts.py, util.py, config.py are T-0's and are FROZEN-BY-CONVENTION for the run: no other ticket may edit them. A ticket that needs a contract change escalates; it does not fork the model.
SHARED SURFACE beyond globs: the SourceKind literal (contracts, T-0) is consumed by T-1 connectors and T-4 DISPLAYABLE_KINDS. T-0 pins the full literal up front so neither can widen it.

SHARED SURFACE beyond globs: config.Settings must ship COMPLETE at T-0 (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, CONTACT_EMAIL, DEBUG_VIEWS, model IDs) or T-1/T-2/T-8 each need to widen it and collide.
